newsitem.title: CUBA: Cubans who stole boat to go to U.S. sentenced.
newsitem.headline: Cubans who stole boat to go to U.S. sentenced.

text.p: A Cuban court on Tuesday sentenced six Cubans to jail terms ranging from eight to 20 years for stealing a tugboat with violence to try to travel to the United States, the Cuban news agency Prensa Latina said.
The case was particularly unusual since the Cubans had been returned to Cuba by U.S. authorities after being picked up at sea by the U.S. Coast Guard when the stolen tugboat capsized.

It appeared to be a first case of repatriated boat people being tried and sentenced since a May 1995 accord providing for such repatriations by U.S. authorities, but it was not immediately possible to confirm this.
Prensa Latina said the six convicted Cubans used a fake bomb, two revolvers and a knife to overpower the captain of the tugboat off the coast of eastern Holguin province in April 1996.

Five of the six were intercepted at sea and returned to Cuba, the news agency said. It did not say what happened to the sixth person brought to trial, or how he came to be tried, although it appeared he was caught before the boat reached the open seas.

The news agency, which did not say where the trial and sentencing took place, said in handing down the sentence the court took into account what it viewed as the "social dangerousness" of the crime, as well as the violence and intimidation used.
The trial of the six was held on February 4, with a pause before sentencing.
Those sentenced have the right to appeal.

Under the May 1995 agreement aimed at halting the flow of illegal rafters from Cuba, the United States undertook to return to Cuba boat people whom it intercepted at sea. Those people intercepted are returned if U.S. authorities believe they will not be persecuted for the act of having tried to leave the country illegally. U.S. authorities monitor the progress of returnees in Cuba to ensure they are not being harassed.
However, Cuba and the United States also undertook in their May 1995 accord to take steps to prevent any use of violence in attempts at illegal immigration.
